summary.intent: Resolve the remaining review findings on PR #75 (emit-release-preview), then audit the codebase for the same classes of bugs (path-flag resolution, error gating, fence scanning, HTML interpolation, unconditional trims) and record the conventions.
summary.outcome: Both #75 findings were marked resolved with references to commit 66e86f752. The audit found only one convention gap, a documentation one: which path flags are workspace-root-relative and which are process-directory-relative. That was documented in architecture/versioning.md, review-finding patterns were appended to the local plan, and the change was committed and pushed to feat/emit-release-preview.

repo: Emit/preview flags (version --emit-preview, compose-pr-body --preview) resolve relative paths from the workspace root; the hidden release subcommand file flags resolve relative to the process directory. This is now documented in docs/architecture/versioning.md.

Markdown fence scanning is centralized in crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/fences.rs. Earlier, has_heading, find_section and headings.rs each had their own scanner and disagreed. New Markdown passes should reuse it.
Only crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs interpolates into raw HTML. Summary titles there are escaped HTML while bullet titles are Markdown, and package names cannot contain markup.
find_section ends a section at any column-0 '## ' or '# ', so rich entries rendered into the committed changelog must be rebased to heading level 4 or deeper, or indented.
version --emit-decision gates on !has_errors, and --emit-preview originally lacked the same guard. Sibling emitters must copy each other's guards.
snapshot aborts on graph errors before writing anything, and release --receipt probes its path before doing work.
Unconditional char trims such as trim_end_matches('#') eat data like 'C#'. Strip only the syntactic form; an ATX closing sequence needs a preceding space.

code.finding: This is the line next to the 'version --emit-decision derives' description. A sentence was added here saying which path flags are workspace-root-relative and which are process-relative.
snapshot checks for graph errors and aborts before writing output. This is the correct error-gating pattern that the preview emitter was missing.

workflow: The trail CLI marks findings resolved with `entire trail finding resolve <id> --branch <branch> -m <msg>`. Each message cites the fix commit and the regression test name.
After fixing a review finding, grep sibling code for the same bug class (path resolution, gates, scanners, HTML interpolation, trims) rather than fixing only the reported instance.
Review learnings are kept in .claude/plans/PLAN-release-notes.md so later work can check them before writing similar code.

friction: The path-flag convention was inconsistent and undocumented, so a flag and its reader could resolve the same path differently until the audit.
Output was piped through `tail -1` and `head` throughout, which hides most command output and makes the commit and push results hard to verify.
open_items: The changelog rebase rule (rich entries rendered into the committed changelog must be level 4 or deeper, or indented) is noted as 'later' and is not yet implemented.
The hidden release subcommands still use process-directory-relative paths; this was documented but not unified with the workspace-root convention.
